paragraphs: Decision center: The work of a dishwasher is to turn hygiene requirements such as separating dirty from clean dishes and cookware and equipment, the washing and sanitizing process, returning and restocking items, and cleaning the back-of-house areas into a washing chain that is visible in the restaurant and cafeteria back of house, can be picked up by co-workers and can be handed over cleanly at the end of the shift — first collect by category and scrape residue and pre-wash, then wash and sanitize and dry according to the process, then return clean dishes and replenish the pass and cabinets and storage, while cleaning equipment and areas and floors and the dining area, taking out the trash and reporting shortages and breakage and equipment anomalies to the shift supervisor. The focus of judgment is not whether you can scrub dishes, but whether every step of the collection—washing—sanitizing—returning—cleaning—handoff chain is clean, timely and checkable, so that the kitchen and the food runners and the storage and the shift supervisor can all continue their work.

Good to try first: Able to stand and walk and lift and bend for long periods without falling behind; willing to follow the standard sequence (sort before washing, wash before sanitizing, no cross-contact between clean and dirty) rather than rushing; able to hold hygiene and safety bottom lines under the time pressure of wet floors and heat and noise and meal peaks; able to work fixed shifts and cooperate with kitchen and food runner and storage colleagues.

Proceed with caution: If you cannot stand for long periods or handle lifting and heat and wet floors and noise, cannot accept repeating the same washing and wiping motions for an entire shift, make mistakes easily when hurried during meal peaks, or are unwilling to follow hard food safety and personal hygiene requirements (health certificate, daily morning check, hand washing and sanitizing, wearing work clothing and hat and protective items), then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: Using the fictional washing area and dish list and process cards provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of arranging a washing and sanitizing sequence by dirty-clean separation, listing an equipment and area cleaning check list, and recording two shortages and one equipment anomaly and writing a handoff. This only verifies whether you are willing to check off the procedure item by item and hand off truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not touch real dishes, food or washing equipment, does not perform real washing, sanitizing or sample retention, and is not equivalent to qualified training or professional qualification.

Decision center: Whether the collection, washing, sanitizing, returning and area cleaning of dishes and cookware from dirty to clean can be organized into a washing chain that front and back colleagues can continue and the shift supervisor can review.

The workplace is the washing area and back of house of restaurants and cafeterias and hotels and central kitchens, and the rhythm is determined by meal peaks and serving speed and the pace of the washing equipment.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: This page is O*NET-SOC 35-9021.00 Dishwashers. Adjacent positions have different duties — dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers are responsible for front-of-house table setting and assisting with serving food and drinks and clearing and cleaning, food preparation workers are responsible for prepping and cutting and portioning, restaurant cooks are responsible for preparing dishes and serving, cleaners and building cleaners are responsible for routine cleaning of buildings and public areas, and food service managers are responsible for store operations and staff and costs. The focus of this occupation is washing and sanitizing and returning and trash removal and material handling in the back of house and washing area. Requirements for cleaning and sanitizing food-contact surfaces and for employee health management are governed by the laws of the relevant jurisdiction and the institution's rules, are not inferred from the job title, and no one may change the washing and sanitizing process on their own or promise hygiene results externally.

Inputs that must be checked: the washing and sanitizing process and water temperature and chemical concentration requirements for the shift, the location of dishware washing and sanitizing and storage facilities, the dirty-clean separation and storage standards for dishes and cookware, the status of washing equipment and hot water and drainage and electricity, the use and storage and labeling of detergents and sanitizers, the shortage and breakage and equipment anomaly list, and the shift supervisor's shift instructions and personal hygiene and morning check requirements. What must not be done: do not skip washing and sanitizing steps or lower water temperature and concentration, do not mix detergents and sanitizers or use them above the stated concentration, do not return unwashed or unsanitized dishes and containers to storage and serving areas, do not store cleaning products together with food and dishes, do not dismantle or repair washing equipment or electrical and drainage facilities on your own, and do not use back-of-house and dining area information or co-workers' personal information for purposes other than service.

The fit judgment should be made by considering whether you can stand and lift for long periods and work under heat and wet floors and noise, whether you can keep motions and records accurate according to the washing and sanitizing sequence, whether you can maintain hygiene and safety standards during meal peaks, whether you can hand off clearly with front and back colleagues, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization boundaries; it should not be replaced by a self-assessment of having done housework or being able to endure hardship; all of these must be confirmed in supervised actual positions and a trial period.

The work object of this occupation is the back of house and washing area of a food service establishment: dishes and glassware and flatware and pots and cookware, washing and sanitizing and storage facilities and equipment, detergents and sanitizers and cleaning supplies, pass and cabinet and refrigerator and storage materials, trash cans and the waste collection area, and dining tables and floors. The output is washing and cleaning results that keep the kitchen and serving and dining running continuously: washing and sanitizing completed by dirty-clean separation and returned to position, clean dishes ready at any time and a tidy washing area and floor, accurately replenished materials and inventory, trash removed, and handover records of shortages and breakage and equipment anomalies. The basis for judgment is the washing and sanitizing process and water temperature and chemical concentration requirements for the shift, dirty-clean separation and storage standards, requirements for the use and storage of detergents and sanitizers, personal hygiene and daily morning check requirements (under the Operation Specifications for Food Safety in Catering Services), and the shift supervisor's on-site instructions — not personal habit or job title.

Judgment one: Are dirty-clean separation and collection in place — are dirty dishes collected by category of dishware and pots and glassware and scraped and pre-washed, are clean and dirty zones separated without cross-contact, and are broken and damaged items separated promptly with safety warnings?

Judgment two: Are washing and sanitizing carried out according to the process — are water temperature and chemical concentration and soaking and rinsing and sanitizing time executed to standard, and is the order of washing before sanitizing followed?

Judgment three: Are returning and replenishing checkable — are clean dishes and cookware returned to the storage and holding area to standard, are pass and cabinet and refrigerator and salad bar materials replenished as needed, and are shortages logged?

Judgment four: Are washing and sanitizing and cleaning facilities and equipment in usable and clean condition — are washing equipment and hot water and drainage and sanitizing facilities checked and cleaned by shift, and are anomalies reported immediately rather than worked around?

The work of dishwashers can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is collection and pre-washing: collect dishes and cookware and glassware by category from the pass and dining area and kitchen, scrape residue and pre-wash and place items according to dirty-clean separation, and handle broken and damaged items with safety warnings, preparing for washing. The second is washing and sanitizing and returning: wash and rinse according to the process and water temperature and chemical concentration and apply sanitizing and drying, draining and holding per procedure, check the washed and sanitized results, return clean dishes and cookware to the storage and holding area, and replenish pass and cabinet and refrigerator and salad bar materials. The third is cleaning and handling and handoff: clean and maintain washing equipment and drain filters and the washing area and floors and trash cans and the waste collection area, clean dining tables and floors, check sanitizing by the specific object and procedure, remove trash to the designated collection area and move and receive and store materials, log shortages and breakage and equipment anomalies, and hand off unfinished items to the next shift. All three work areas proceed under the institution's processes and food safety requirements, and the rhythm is determined by meal peaks and serving speed and the pace of the equipment.

paragraphs: Dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers (35-9011.00)

In the front of house, set tables and restock to standard, greet guests and arrange seating, serve food and drinks according to orders and clear and clean, assist with cashier checkout and log shortages and breakage.

Scenarios and duties differ: dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers face customers in the front of house and complete table setting and serving food and drinks and clearing according to the service process; the occupation on this page completes the washing and sanitizing and returning and area cleaning of dishes and cookware in the back of house and washing area, and is not responsible for greeting, serving or order service.

If you want to face customers directly and enter through table setting and serving, you can follow the dining room and cafeteria attendant and bartender helper path; if you want to do washing and sanitizing and cleaning to standard in the back of house, the occupation on this page is a closer fit.
Food preparation workers (35-2021.00)
In the kitchen, complete prepping and washing and cutting and portioning and serving preparation according to recipes, and take responsibility for ingredient handling and hygiene specifications.

Scope of duties differs: food preparation workers undertake production operations such as prepping and cutting and portioning; the occupation on this page only washes or pre-treats various foods in preparation for cooking or serving, and washes and sanitizes dishes and cookware according to the process, and does not bear responsibility for cutting and portioning or product quality.

If you want to work in ingredient handling and cutting, you can follow the food preparation worker direction and check hygiene and operation training requirements; if you want to work around washing and sanitizing and cleaning, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
Restaurant cooks (35-2014.00)

Technical responsibility differs: restaurant cooks are responsible for dish technique and taste and serving time; the occupation on this page is responsible for the washing and sanitizing and returning of dishware and back-of-house cleaning, and does not bear dish preparation or recipe decisions.

If you prefer back-of-house preparation and output, you can choose the restaurant cook direction; if you would rather work in washing and cleaning and handling, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
Cleaners and building cleaners (37-2011.00)

Objects and scenarios differ: cleaners and building cleaners face general cleaning of buildings and public areas; the occupation on this page faces the food service back of house and washing area, must follow the washing and sanitizing and cleaning requirements for food-contact surfaces and dishware, and is bound by employee health management requirements.

If you want to work in building and public area cleaning, you can choose the cleaner and building cleaner direction; if you want to do washing and sanitizing in a food service back of house according to food safety requirements, the occupation on this page is a closer fit.
Laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand (53-7062.00)

Content differs: manual handling positions are mainly lifting and loading and unloading; the occupation on this page is mainly washing and sanitizing and returning dishware and area cleaning, and handling and receiving and storing materials are only part of it, and must follow the separation and hygiene requirements for food and cleaning supplies.

If you want to focus on handling and loading and unloading, you can choose the manual handling and material moving direction and check safety and operation requirements; if you want to work around washing and sanitizing, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
Food service managers (11-9051.00)

Level and responsibility differ: food service managers are responsible for operations and staff and costs and compliance; the occupation on this page bears execution responsibility for back-of-house washing and cleaning, and does not bear scheduling and cost and purchasing and hygiene management decisions.

If you want to move toward operations and staff and cost management, you can follow the food service manager path and build up management and compliance abilities; if you want to focus on back-of-house execution, the occupation on this page is more suitable.

entries.question: What does a dishwasher do every day?

entries.answer: This occupation is an execution position for washing and cleaning in the food service back of house and washing area: responsible for washing and sanitizing and returning dishware and cookware, trash removal, material handling and area and dining area cleaning; dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers are responsible in the front of house for table setting and assisting with serving food and drinks and clearing and cleaning; food preparation workers are responsible for prepping and cutting and portioning; restaurant cooks are responsible for dish preparation and serving. Authorization and outputs differ, and the positions cannot be swapped by name.

entries.answer: AI and information systems can assist with scheduling, monitoring washing equipment water temperature and chemical dosing, and dishware and material inventory and cleaning check lists, but cannot replace dirty-clean separation and on-site judgment, confirmation of washing and sanitizing results, personnel health management and food safety responsibility; this page has no evidence of adoption rates or substitution timelines for this occupation.
entries.question: How will AI affect this job?

entries.answer: Dishwashers and washing and sanitizing and storage facilities, water temperature and chemical dosing monitoring and recording, inventory and check list tools, and scheduling systems; these tools improve efficiency, but confirmation of washing and sanitizing results, handling of equipment jams and hygiene and safety standards remain the responsibility of people.

description.text: Dishwashers (O*NET-SOC 35-9021.00) complete the washing and sanitizing and returning of dishes and cookware, trash removal, material handling and storage, and cleaning and sanitizing of the washing area and dining area in the back of house and washing area of restaurants, canteens, hotels and central kitchens; they work according to dirty-clean separation and the process and water temperature and chemical concentration and check the results, and inventory and hand off by shift. United States scope: the 2025 wage data median annual wage is 34,810 US dollars (median hourly wage 16.73 US dollars), with annual percentiles of 26,200／29,690／34,810／37,440／42,860 US dollars; employment was about 477,700 in 2024, the 2024—2034 projection is little or no change (slower than average), with about 76,800 projected openings; the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 and the interest code is RC. Chinese mainland: there is no uniform access-type professional qualification, and work in contact with ready-to-eat food requires an annual health examination and a health certificate and passing the daily morning check; public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage scope, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.name: Dishwashers
subject.summary: Dishwashers (United States side, O*NET-SOC 35-9021.00) are an execution position for washing and cleaning in the food service back of house and washing area: washing dishes and glassware and flatware and pots, and keeping the kitchen work area and equipment and utensils clean and orderly; collecting and scraping and pre-washing by category from the pass and dining area and kitchen, and completing washing and rinsing and sanitizing and drying according to the process and water temperature and chemical concentration and checking the results; returning clean dishes and cookware to the storage and holding area and replenishing pass and cabinet and refrigerator and salad bar materials; washing or pre-treating various foods in preparation for cooking or serving, removing trash by category to the designated collection area, handling and receiving and storing materials, preparing and packing single-portion utensil settings and setting banquet tables, and cleaning and sanitizing the dining area including tables. United States scope: for this occupation the 2025 wage data median annual wage is 34,810 US dollars (median hourly wage 16.73 US dollars), with annual percentiles of 26,200／29,690／34,810／37,440／42,860 US dollars (hourly percentiles 12.59／14.27／16.73／18.00／20.61); the O*NET summary page gives employment of about 477,700 in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of little or no change (slower than average) and about 76,800 projected job openings; the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), the education feedback is 56% high school or equivalent and 43% less than high school and 1% some college no degree, related experience is partly none required and partly several months to a year, with on-the-job training from a few days to a year; the interest code is RC; the work context includes in a controlled indoor environment every day 84%, face-to-face discussions every day 62%, continuous standing 45%, continuous use of hands 53%, continuous repetitive motions 25%, wearing common protective or safety equipment every day 56%, time pressure every day 47%, teamwork extremely important 31%, coordinating or leading others extremely important 44%, very high responsibility for the health and safety of other workers 62%, and working hours regular (fixed shifts) 85%. Chinese mainland scope: this occupation has no uniform access-type professional qualification; personnel working in contact with ready-to-eat food should undergo an annual health examination and obtain a health certificate before taking up a post under Article forty-five of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, and catering service providers establish a daily morning check system and personal hygiene and dishware washing and sanitizing and holding requirements under the Operation Specifications for Food Safety in Catering Services (State Administration for Market Regulation Announcement No. 12 of 2018, effective 2018-10-01), and dishes, drinking utensils and containers holding ready-to-eat food should be washed and sanitized before use. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage scope corresponding to this occupation, and this page truthfully retains the gap.
